summary: Sicheng Liang worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Beijing Huiwen Middle School, Tsinghua University (~1915–1923), and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (~1924–1927). He held a post at Peking University (~1931–1932).
Sidney Lee studied at the City of London School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882). He held an academic post at Queen Mary University of London from circa 1913 to 1924.

Siegbert Hummel worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tübingen, Rostock, Munich, and Leipzig (PhD 1932–1938), under Erkes, Schubert, Wedemeyer, and Weller. He served as Curator of the Asian Department at Grassi Museum (1947–1955).

Siegfried Behrsing studied at Greifswald, Tübingen, and Leipzig (PhD 1924–1930) under scholars including Heller, von Garbe, and Weller. He worked at Leipzig, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and as Professor and Director at Humboldt University (1953–1969).

Siegfried Goldschmidt worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Humboldt University, Göttingen, Paris, and Tübingen (PhD 1867) under Weber, Benfey, and von Roth. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Strasbourg (1871, 1881).

Indologist Siegfried Lienhard studied at Vienna (Dr. phil. 1946–1949), Paris, and Stockholm. He held posts at Göttingen, Banaras Hindu University, Kiel (1962–1968), and Stockholm University (1958–1962, 1968–1990), and was General Secretary of the IASS (~1984–1990).

Siglinde Dietz specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied under Frank-Richard Hamm and completed her PhD under Michael Hahn at the University of Bonn by 1980. She was affiliated with the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).

Linguist Siew-Yue Killingley earned an M.A. from the University of Malaya (~1961–1964) and a Ph.D. from SOAS (~1968–1972). She taught at St Mary's College, Fenham (1972–1980) and the University of Newcastle (~1974–1985).

Sigmund Feist was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1885–1888, Ph.D.) and later served as Director of the Reichenheim Orphanage (1906–1935).
Signe Cohen specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied under Ludo Rocher and serves as a professor at the University of Missouri.

Signe Howell, working in religious studies and other fields, studied at SOAS University of London (~1974–1976) and the University of Oxford (~1977–1980). She was appointed Professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Sigrid Westphal-Hellbusch studied at Humboldt University (PhD 1935–1940) and held posts there (1946, 1951–1953), Museum Fünf Kontinente (1940–1945), Free University of Berlin (1956–1970), and Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1970–1976), working in Indology and other fields.

Sigurd Lindquist was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Uppsala University (1914–1932, Ph.D.) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, and was appointed Docent in the psychology and history of religions there in 1934.

Silvia Luraghi, a scholar in linguistics and Indology, studied at the University of Turin (Laurea 1978–1982) and University of Pavia (PhD 1983–1987). She held posts at Turin (~1992–1999), Roma Tre (~1998–1999), and Pavia (~1999).
Silvio Trovanelli, who worked in philosophy and Indology, completed a law degree at the University of Bologna in 1883 and later served there as a docent of juridical philosophy.

Silvio Vita, a specialist in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton. He taught at Naples "L'Orientale" and Rome, and was Director of the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2001–2023).

Simo Parpola, a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology, studied at Helsinki (PhD 1961–1968), the Pontifical Biblical Institute, and the British Museum. He held posts at Heidelberg, Chicago, and the University of Helsinki (Docent 1973–1976; Professor 1978).

Indologist Simon Cubelic studied at Heidelberg (PhD 2010–2017) and Humboldt University. He worked at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2024), Heidelberg University (2024–2025), and was appointed Professor of Modern Indology at Munich (2025).

Simon Matthews Edwin Kempson studied at Cheltenham College and Gonville and Caius College. A scholar in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Bareilly College, University of Calcutta, Cambridge (1879–1881), and Staff College, Camberley (1882–1883).

Simon P. James works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as a Tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as a Lecturer in Philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
